Radius of the loop, $r=1 \mathrm{ cm}=0.01 \mathrm{ m}$

Which is equal to the electric field due to remaining part of wire as per charge conservation.
$\therefore$ Charge of the part $l^{\prime}, Q^{\prime}=l^{\prime} \lambda=\frac{2 \pi \times 10^{-6} \times 10^{-4}}{2 \pi}$
=10^{-10} $\mathrm{C}\therefore$ Electric field at centre, $\begin{aligned} E & =\frac{Q^{\prime}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r^2}\\
E & =\frac{10^{-10} \times 9 \times 10^9}{(0.01)^2}\\
& =9 \times10^3 \mathrm{ N}/ \mathrm{C}
\end{aligned}$

Charge on sphere,

questions.q: Two charged identical metal spheres $A$ and $B$ repel each other with a force of $3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ N}$. Another identical wncharged sphere $C$ is touched with sphere $A$ and then it is placed mid-way between $A$ and $B$. Then, the magnitude of net force on $C$ is
questions.solution:
Spheres $A and B$ have the same charge of same nature. When uncharged sphere $C$ is touched with sphere $A$, then charge is transferred to $C$ and this charge is equally divided between two spheres.
Let initially the charge on spheres $A and B$ is $q$. Initially, the repelling force between charged spheres $A and B=3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ N}$ When, sphere $C$, is placed between charged spheres $A and B$, then the force between $A and C$, F_{A C}=$\frac{k \frac{q}{2} \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}$ Similarly, between $B and C$ F_{B C}=$\frac{k q \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}$ The magnitude of net force on $C, F^{\prime}=F_{B C}-F_{A C}$ Also F=$\frac{k q \times q}{r^2}=3 \times10^{-5} \mathrm{ N}$ So, $\frac{F}{F_{B C}-F_{A C}}=\frac{\left(k q^2 / r^2\right)}{k\left[\frac{q \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}-\frac{q / 2 \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}\right]}$ Here, $\quad F=3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{ N}, F_{B C}-F_{A C}=F^{\prime} \begin{aligned}$& $\frac{3 \times 10^{-5}}{F^{\prime}}$& =$\frac{1}{2-1}=\frac{1}{1}=1 \\ \therefore \quad \text{$ and $} F^{\prime} \text{ and } =3 \times10^{-5} \mathrm{ N} \end{aligned}$

Energy stored, $E \propto q^2\begin{aligned} \frac{E_1}{E_2} & =\left(\frac{q_2}{q_2}\right)^2 \\ \frac{100}{121} & =\left(\frac{q}{q+2}\right)^2 \\ \left(\frac{10}{11}\right)^2 & =\left(\frac{q}{q+2}\right)^2 \\ \frac{10}{11} & =\frac{q}{q+2} \\ \Rightarrow 10 q+20 & =11 q \\ q & =20 \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
